About Me

Hi, I am Jake Amaral, a third year computer science student at the University of Florida. This past summer, I took the opportunity of a lifetime to travel to Cape Town, South Africa to assist a nonprofit in their everyday administrative tasks, where I've grown as a computer scientist and beyond!

When I'm not coding or designing, I love producing music, travelling to a new place, and playing a nice 18 holes of golf.

Projects

Selected work

Spatial Math

April 2026 – Present · C#, Unity

A real-time 3D graphing calculator built in Unity that compiles equations you type into surfaces you can walk around and inspect.

  • Compiles user-typed equations into executable functions supporting variables, nested functions, operator precedence, and implicit multiplication.
  • Procedural mesh generation that samples equations across a configurable grid of 3,700+ vertices, triangulating them into a colored, height-mapped surface rendered with Unity's core Mesh API.
  • Clicking any point on the graph shows the slope and a matching flat tangent plane at that spot.
  • Currently laying the groundwork for a virtual reality version that helps students explore math visually.
UnityC#Mesh APIVR

Safe Cities Project Management Platform

Internship · Production

The internal platform Safe Cities staff use to run their programmes, built with a team of four for an organization of 30+ people.

  • Built features in Next.js, TypeScript, PostgreSQL, Supabase, and Drizzle ORM.
  • Integrated Clerk authentication with role-based access and webhook syncing between the auth provider and the app database.
  • Wired up Google OAuth 2.0 and the Calendar API, and added a calendar_events table through Drizzle ORM with relational links to the existing pages and programmes tables.
  • Revived a paused Supabase instance, migrated the data, and added a GitHub Actions keep-alive cron so it never goes dormant again.
